text:
laura: FYI seeing a weird cluster-wide blip in attach latency + nvme_io_err counters in us-east1-b starting ~13:07 UTC. GPU jobs stuck in Pending due to attach timeouts :frowning:
infra-bot: alert: nvme.errors.count > 1000 over 7m on region us-east1-b, attach_latency.p95 > 600ms
chris: digging into node gnode-ff12, dmesg shows a repeated pattern: `nvme_core: I/O error, submit failed` then a flurry of small writes from /var/tmp/test-runner
riley: that aligns with tempstore churn. test-runner creates lots of 4K files then deletes them in parallel. small_write_iops spikes correlate with nvme err increments
tay: can we confirm if it's a firmware regression? i checked recent fw push last night but only for ap-southeast nodes, not us-east
chris: not fw. SMART shows elevated write amplification on some drives and a lot of write latency tail. I think overlayfs rename+fsync pattern from tempstore causes heavy write amplification on our NVMe hotstripes
laura: so two coupled issues: aggressive small-write patterns + cleaner/janitor delete parallelism causing sudden fanout and fsync storms -> nvme controller errors -> attach stalls
riley: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) throttle janitor deletes in affected pools 2) cordon highest-error hosts and migrate pending attaches off them 3) enable driver-level write coalescing (soft) on tempstore writers if available
chris: howto for (1): `kubectl -n infra set env deployment/tempstore-janitor DELETE_CONCURRENCY=2 DELETE_RATE=200` and restart. will do a canary on 2 nodes first
ops-bot: runbook step executed: canary env patch queued (chris). See /runbooks/tempstore-janitor-throttle
laura: (2) command: `kubectl cordon gnode-ff12 gnode-ff13` then trigger graceful pod reschedule for in-flight attaches
riley: (3) short-term code toggle exists: TEMPSTORE_COALESCE=1 for writer side; we can flip via ConfigMap but risky without load test
tay: alternative quick kernel tweak: increase `nvme_max_io_qdepth`? iirc default is fine but we can limit qdepth per controller to reduce overload. that requires node-level change via sysctl wrapper
chris: i'll run janitor canary now. posting logs here.
chris: deploy: tempstore-janitor env updated on canary nodes
chris: 13:17 UTC -> small_write_iops on canary dropped 78k -> 19k; nvme err delta slowed. attach p95 on canary nodes improved 640ms -> 260ms
laura: good. proceed to roll to all affected pools but in waves of 5 nodes so we don't cause mass reschedule
oncall-bot: scheduled: tempstore-janitor throttled across us-east1-b in batches at 13:25, 13:30, 13:35 UTC (chris)
riley: also gated the heavy test-runner jobs via a short ACL: set parallelism=1 for `test-runner/*` in staging pools
chris: after rolling throttle, cluster metrics: small_write_iops overall down 85%, nvme err rate near zero, attach p95 back to 180ms baseline. still seeing a handful of nodes with persistent write latency -> flagged for offline replace
laura: follow-ups: 1) add an auto-safemode: if attach_latency.p95 > 500ms then janitor automatically scales DELETE_CONCURRENCY down to 1 2) long-term: add coalescer to tempstore writer and tune overlayfs commit intervals 3) schedule a firmware health sweep for the flagged drives
tay: i'll own the safemode RFC and include a simulated load test
riley: i'll open INF-8421 with reproduction steps + grep logs + top writers list
laura: ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421 (investigate tempstore write amplification + nvme error coupling)
infra-bot: incident resolved: metrics stabilized at 13:48 UTC, auto-incident closed
